=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 172-246 (second `if ! command -v _embed_input_file` block)
  Problem: The second `_embed_input_file` fallback block introduced by this PR is unreachable dead code. The first fallback block at lines 95-168 already defines `_embed_input_file` when it is missing, so the guard condition `if ! command -v _embed_input_file` at line 172 will never be true. The two blocks differ in meaningful ways: the active first block validates numeric state with `[[ =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]`, validates file size is numeric, and reads only `cap+1` bytes of the target file; the dead second block uses bare `[ -n ]` checks and reads the entire file into memory via `Path.read_bytes()`. The dead block also imports `from pathlib import Path` which the active block does not use.
  Why it fails at runtime: The second block can never execute, so any behavioral intent it was supposed to deliver (different validation strictness, full-file memory read) is silently absent. This is a forward-merge conflict-resolution artifact where both sides of the merge contributed functionally equivalent but implementation-different fallback blocks, and the second one was appended after the first instead of replacing it. The dead code is also a maintenance hazard: future readers may edit the second block thinking it runs, or may add a third block following the same broken pattern.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh
  Line or code reference: line 1411 (structured-output validator) and line 1696 (refusal short-circuit)
  Problem: Both refusal checks now only inspect the first non-empty line of the editor output, piped through `printf '%s\n' "${_tmp_output_first_nonempty_line}" | grep -qiE`. The `_REFUSAL_REGEX` pattern is anchored with `^` and `$` on each alternation branch, meaning it matches only a standalone refusal line. In the previous code the grep ran against the entire file, so a genuine refusal on line 2 or later (after a blank line or preamble) would still be caught. Now it must appear on the very first non-empty line. This is the intended design trade-off (avoiding false positives from quoted refusal examples in structured success output), but it introduces a gap: if a model emits whitespace then a refusal, the short-circuit will fire; but if a model emits any non-empty non-refusal text before the refusal, the short-circuit is bypassed and the attempt falls through to the generic failure path instead of setting `editor_refused.flag`.
  Why it fails at runtime: A model that emits a preamble (e.g. diagnostic prose or a partial tool invocation) followed by a refusal would not trigger the short-circuit, causing the editor summary to use the generic "unavailable (editor fallback)" label instead of "model refused (safety filter)". This changes downstream alert routing (`EDITOR_NOOP_REFUSAL` would not be set) and the e2e poller would not emit the refusal-specific warning. The practical impact is low because OpenAI refusals typically appear on line 1, but the behavioral contract has narrowed.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: line 8994 (`_std_cached_head_sha=$(... jq -r '(.head_sha // .head.sha // .headRefOid // empty)' ...)`)
  Problem: The jq `// empty` operator correctly eliminates JSON `null` values, but if the GraphQL field contains the JSON string `"null"` (the four-character literal string, not the null value), jq will return the string `null` which passes the downstream `if $hs != ""` check and gets embedded into `_STD_ITER_PR_JSON_CACHED` as `"sha":"null"`. The guard logic that matches by SHA would then compare against the string `null` and never match a real workflow run, failing safe (no push). This is a harmless edge case but worth documenting.
  Why it fails at runtime: No actual failure — the guard fails safe (no empty-commit push when SHA comparison never matches). The worst outcome is a missed recovery opportunity, not a race.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- Requirement: "Automated forward-merge of stable into main failed due to merge conflicts. Resolve the conflicts and merge this PR so the bug fix on stable is also present on main."
  Expected change site: The PR description lists 19 conflicting files. The merge commit `bc4f246` resolves conflicts across 94 files. The AI autofix run (last-run diff) touched 6 files to fix post-merge issues. The remaining files were already resolved in the initial merge commit.
  Evidence of absence: Not a gap — the merge commit itself resolved the bulk of the conflicts, and the AI autofix addressed regression hazards introduced by the resolution. The full PR diff shows all 94 files changed in the merge commit are present.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: N/A — already satisfied by the merge commit.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 1407-1414 (structured-output validation), lines 1682-1699 (refusal short-circuit)
  Problem: The `_tmp_output_first_nonempty_line` capture uses `grep -m1 -vE '^[[:space:]]*$' "${tmp_output}"` which can produce an empty string on all-whitespace output. The subsequent grep pipelines then operate on empty input, potentially producing unexpected results.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the editor output starts with blank lines (common when the model adds diagnostic prose before the structured output), the first non-empty line capture returns empty, and the refusal regex check against empty input silently succeeds (no match), potentially allowing a refusal that appears later to go undetected, or failing to properly classify valid output.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 8983-8998
  Problem: The jq extraction for head SHA uses multiple fallbacks `(.head_sha // .head.sha // .headRefOid // empty)` but does not validate that the result is a valid SHA format before embedding it into the cached JSON payload. A malformed or whitespace-padded value could be passed through.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the GraphQL response contains an unexpected field format or whitespace, the downstream code that reads `.head.sha` may receive an invalid value, causing the blank-head_branch in-flight review guard to fail matching.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
